case_scope: BNPL and earned-wage-access fragmented credit visibility

household_market_extraction_gate.note: BNPL volume/user/frequency metrics and EWA regulatory status show a live visibility problem: useful liquidity cannot be certified unless total obligations, fees, refunds, disputes, and payroll priority are observable together.

bnpl_fragmented_credit_visibility.note: The CFPB BNPL market report gives provider-market metrics, but the enforcement posture and product-rights perimeter remain too volatile to treat BNPL as ordinary card credit.

earned_wage_access_fee_visibility.note: The 2025 EWA advisory opinion treats covered EWA as outside Regulation Z credit and narrows finance-charge treatment; certification must therefore prove fee/tip visibility and payroll-priority effects directly.

source_family.note: Regulator-facing product data remains a measurement gate.

household_market_remedy_access.note: Refund, dispute, hardship, payroll-deduction, and chargeback remedies are not proven across providers and cannot be inferred from product usefulness.

consumer_credit_fee_drag.note: BNPL and EWA must be scored against the full household-debt stack, not as stand-alone low-dollar products.

proof_debt: repeat use for groceries, utilities, medical, rent, and other necessities
late-fee, charge-off, refund, and dispute outcomes by provider
EWA expedited-fee/tip incidence and payroll-deduction priority
credit-file visibility, nonreporting, and debt-collection transition after default

gate_16_household_market_extraction.why: BNPL/EWA may help with timing, but Gate 16 cannot pass until total obligation load, fee/tip burden, and dispute/refund conversion are proven across providers.

gate_10_measurement_uncertainty.why: The central risk is hidden aggregation across providers and payroll rails.

evidence_debt_register.question: cross-provider BNPL obligation stacking
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Require household-level total-obligation data across providers and payment rails before treating BNPL as benign liquidity.

evidence_debt_register.question: repeat use for necessities
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Separate discretionary retail use from repeated necessity financing, including groceries, utilities, medical bills, rent-adjacent payments, and car repairs.

evidence_debt_register.question: refund and dispute outcomes
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Measure whether consumers can stop payments or obtain refunds when merchants fail, goods are returned, or BNPL provider/merchant responsibility is unclear.

evidence_debt_register.question: EWA fee/tip and payroll priority incidence
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Quantify expedited fees, tips, employer-integrated payroll deductions, and next-paycheck shortfalls after EWA use.

evidence_debt_register.question: credit-file and collection transition
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Track whether nonreported obligations surface only after default, debt collection, bank-account loss, or specialty-reporting harm.

policy_pathway: Treat BNPL and EWA as household-total-load rails rather than isolated transactions.
Require total obligation visibility, fee/tip disclosure, refund and dispute pausing, payroll-deduction limits, hardship pauses, and provider-level public reporting before moving from watch to pass.
